lessons.title: Training versus inference
lessons.subtitle: Week 3: Training and generalisation
lessons.body:
Training adjusts model parameters using data. Inference uses a trained model to produce an output. Ordinary prompting does not mean you are personally retraining the model.

Offline practice: Draw separate training and inference diagrams for a message classifier. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Training adjusts model parameters using data. Inference uses a trained model to produce an output. Ordinary prompting does not mean you are personally retraining the model.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Training and test examples
lessons.subtitle: Week 3: Training and generalisation
lessons.body:
Training examples help fit a model. Separate evaluation examples help estimate performance on unfamiliar data. Test data should not be used repeatedly to choose improvements.

Offline practice: Split twelve fictional examples into development and final-test groups and explain the separation. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Training examples help fit a model. Separate evaluation examples help estimate performance on unfamiliar data. Test data should not be used repeatedly to choose improvements.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.

lessons.title: Overfitting
lessons.subtitle: Week 3: Training and generalisation
lessons.body:
Overfitting occurs when a model fits training examples too closely and performs poorly on new examples. Memorising practice answers is different from understanding a rule.

Offline practice: Invent a sorting rule that fits three examples but fails on a fourth. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Overfitting occurs when a model fits training examples too closely and performs poorly on new examples. Memorising practice answers is different from understanding a rule.

lessons.title: Underfitting
lessons.subtitle: Week 3: Training and generalisation
lessons.body:
Underfitting occurs when a model cannot capture important patterns. A rule that predicts the same outcome for every input may miss useful differences.

Offline practice: Compare an always-the-same prediction with a rule using one relevant feature. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Underfitting occurs when a model cannot capture important patterns. A rule that predicts the same outcome for every input may miss useful differences.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: A baseline comparison
lessons.subtitle: Week 3: Training and generalisation
lessons.body:
A baseline is a simple reference method. A complicated model should be compared with a relevant baseline using the same evaluation conditions.

Offline practice: Compare a fictional AI revision plan with a simple fifteen-minute daily checklist using a clear success measure. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A baseline is a simple reference method. A complicated model should be compared with a relevant baseline using the same evaluation conditions.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
